reference.source: Stiehm's Immunologic Disorders / IUIS classification of inborn errors of immunity
clinicalPearls: Presents as a disorder of immune dysregulation combining autoimmunity, lymphoproliferation and a variable degree of immunodeficiency rather than pure infection susceptibility
Common features include autoimmune cytopenias, enteropathy with chronic diarrhoea, and lymphocytic infiltration of the lungs, gut, liver, marrow and central nervous system
Progressive hypogammaglobulinaemia frequently develops, so the phenotype can overlap with and be misdiagnosed as common variable immunodeficiency
Respiratory disease may take the form of granulomatous-lymphocytic interstitial lung disease
Penetrance is incomplete and expressivity highly variable, so asymptomatic carriers occur within affected families
Inheritance is autosomal dominant, resulting from heterozygous loss-of-function variants that reduce the dose of functional CTLA-4 protein
There is an increased risk of lymphoma and of end-organ autoimmune damage over time
CTLA4-Ig fusion therapy (abatacept) can replace the missing inhibitory signal and control severe dysregulation, and haematopoietic stem cell transplantation is used in refractory disease
reference.pathophysiology: CTLA-4 is an inhibitory receptor expressed by regulatory and activated T cells that outcompetes the co-stimulatory receptor CD28 for the ligands CD80 and CD86 and removes them from antigen-presenting cells by transendocytosis, thereby restraining T-cell activation. Heterozygous loss-of-function variants leave insufficient CTLA-4 protein (haploinsufficiency), impairing regulatory T-cell function and allowing unchecked effector T-cell activation and lymphocytic infiltration of multiple organs. The resulting loss of tolerance manifests as widespread autoimmunity and lymphoproliferation, while progressive B-cell dysfunction produces hypogammaglobulinaemia and susceptibility to infection.
additionalInvestigations: Lymphocyte subsets and quantification of regulatory T cells
Flow cytometry for CTLA-4 protein expression and transendocytosis function where available
Serum immunoglobulins and specific antibody responses documenting evolving hypogammaglobulinaemia
Autoantibody screen and direct antiglobulin test for autoimmune cytopenias
CTLA4 gene sequencing for heterozygous loss-of-function variants
Organ-directed imaging and biopsy for interstitial lung disease or enteropathy
redFlags: New or progressive neurological deficit from CNS lymphocytic infiltration
Rapidly enlarging lymphadenopathy or organomegaly suggesting lymphoma
Severe autoimmune cytopenia with bleeding or profound anaemia
Progressive breathlessness from interstitial lung disease
reference.prognosis: The disorder is chronic and often progressive with cumulative autoimmune organ damage and a raised lymphoma risk; targeted CTLA4-Ig replacement and, in severe cases, transplantation can achieve substantial disease control and improve outlook.
pitfalls: Diagnosing common variable immunodeficiency and stopping short of genetic testing that reveals a treatable pathway defect
Overlooking asymptomatic carriers because of incomplete penetrance
Attributing multi-organ infiltration to sarcoidosis or malignancy without immunological evaluation
Failing to distinguish it from the phenotypically similar LRBA deficiency
Delaying targeted therapy until irreversible organ damage has occurred
